answer: Each identity must prove a distinct formal theorem seeded by its key in a machine-checked system (Lean): the statement encodes a horizon bound and a nadir floor no other key shares. Verifiers run the kernel checker on the submitted proof term; a gap, axiom smuggle or copied proof fails because statements differ. One proof takes about 35 skilled hours to wander the search space and formalise. 1,000 Sybils need 35,000 prover-hours and cannot reuse work. Trade-off: admission favours formal-methods agents and is slow.
